Feature Definition: Standard deviation of typing speed measured in words per minute across a monitoring session. Captures inconsistency in keystroke timing.
Published Source: Rempel et al. — Effect of keyboard keyswitch make force on applied force and finger flexor muscle activity
Values or Distributions in Source: Typing speed varies significantly under physical and cognitive fatigue conditions
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Cognitive fatigue causes erratic and inconsistent typing patterns; fatigued workers show higher WPM variance
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: normal(14 std=8) | Medium: normal(24 std=10) | Low: normal(38 std=12)
Evidence-Based or Assumption: Partially evidence-based — mean values assumed; distribution shape (normal) is evidence-based
Notes: Mean values of 14/24/38 WPM variation are author assumptions. Research confirms the directional relationship (fatigue = more variation) but does not specify exact numerical thresholds for Low/Medium/High risk categories.

Feature Definition: Standard deviation of typing speed measured in words per minute across a monitoring session.
Published Source: Bergadano et al. — User authentication through keystroke dynamics
Authors: Bergadano F / Gunetti D / Picardi C
Journal/Publisher: ACM Transactions on Information and System Security
Values or Distributions in Source: Inter-key timing intervals follow consistent patterns in unfatigued users and become erratic under load
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Keystroke dynamics change measurably under cognitive load and stress conditions
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: normal(14 std=8) | Medium: normal(24 std=10) | Low: normal(38 std=12)

Feature Definition: Standard deviation of typing speed across session.
Published Source: Revell and Stanton — Mental workload measurement review
Values or Distributions in Source: Mental workload measurement techniques show behavioural indicators of fatigue in computer interaction tasks
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Increased mental workload reduces typing consistency and speed regularity
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: normal(14 std=8) | Medium: normal(24 std=10) | Low: normal(38 std=12)

Feature Definition: Fraction of total session duration during which no keyboard or mouse activity is detected. Expressed as a percentage.
Published Source: Gallup — State of the Global Workplace Report
Values or Distributions in Source: Actively disengaged employees report spending more than 50% of workday on non-productive activities
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Disengaged and burned-out employees exhibit significantly higher idle computer time compared to engaged workers
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(58 to 92) | Medium: uniform(28 to 58) | Low: uniform(5 to 28)
Evidence-Based or Assumption: Partially evidence-based — 50%+ threshold from Gallup; exact boundaries are author assumptions
Notes: Gallup reports >50% non-productive time for disengaged workers. The 58% lower bound for High Risk and 28% upper bound for Low Risk are author design decisions based on this finding. Link: https://www.gallup.com/workplace/349484/state-of-the-global-workplace.aspx

Feature Definition: Fraction of session with no activity.
Published Source: Sonnentag — Recovery work engagement and proactive behavior
Values or Distributions in Source: Recovery and non-work activity are essential to maintaining work engagement and preventing depletion
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Lack of psychological detachment from work is associated with fatigue and reduced engagement
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(58 to 92) | Medium: uniform(28 to 58) | Low: uniform(5 to 28)

Feature Definition: Total continuous computer session time measured from first login activity to last activity without a break exceeding 5 minutes.
Published Source: Pega et al. — Global burdens of ischemic heart disease and stroke attributable to long working hours
Values or Distributions in Source: Working 55+ hours per week (11 hours per day for 5-day week) increases stroke risk by 35% and heart disease by 17%
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Long working hours are directly associated with burnout physical and mental health deterioration
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(10.5 to 15.5) | Medium: uniform(7.5 to 10.5) | Low: uniform(4.5 to 7.5)
Evidence-Based or Assumption: Evidence-based — 10-hour threshold directly from WHO/ILO joint study
Notes: 10.5 hour lower bound for High Risk derived from WHO/ILO 55+ hours per week finding (55/5=11 hours per day). This is the most directly evidence-grounded feature in the dataset. Link: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0160412021002208

Published Source: WHO/ILO Joint Estimate — Long working hours increasing deaths from heart disease and stroke
Values or Distributions in Source: Working 55+ hours per week significantly increases risk of occupational burnout and health outcomes
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Overwork is a primary documented cause of burnout as defined in ICD-11
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(10.5 to 15.5) | Medium: uniform(7.5 to 10.5) | Low: uniform(4.5 to 7.5)

Feature Definition: Custom index measuring variance in break timing and frequency during a work session. 0 = perfectly regular breaks every 90 minutes. 10 = no breaks detected.
Published Source: Kleitman — Basic rest-activity cycle 22 years later
Values or Distributions in Source: Humans have a natural 90-120 minute ultradian performance cycle requiring rest between peaks
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Ignoring ultradian rest cycles causes accumulating cognitive fatigue directly linked to burnout
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(6.5 to 10.0) | Medium: uniform(3.0 to 6.5) | Low: uniform(0.5 to 3.0)
Evidence-Based or Assumption: Directional relationship evidence-based — 90-minute cycle is established; 0-10 scale and thresholds are author design
Notes: The 90-minute cycle is well established. The 0-10 scale itself is designed for this project. The threshold of 6.5 for High Risk (representing 3+ hours without a break) is an author assumption based on the established cycle. Link: https://academic.oup.com/sleep/article/5/4/311/2753136

Feature Definition: Variance in break timing and frequency.
Published Source: Ariga and Lleras — Brief and rare mental breaks keep you focused
Values or Distributions in Source: Brief deactivation and reactivation of task goals prevents vigilance decrements during prolonged work
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Absence of regular short breaks leads to sustained attention fatigue and reduced cognitive performance
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(6.5 to 10.0) | Medium: uniform(3.0 to 6.5) | Low: uniform(0.5 to 3.0)

Values or Distributions in Source: 25-minute focused work intervals followed by 5-minute breaks optimise cognitive performance
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Regular timed breaks prevent mental fatigue accumulation during knowledge work
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(6.5 to 10.0) | Medium: uniform(3.0 to 6.5) | Low: uniform(0.5 to 3.0)

Feature Definition: Absolute difference between the employee's current login time and their established baseline login time (9AM default). Measures schedule drift.
Published Source: Roenneberg et al. — Social jetlag and obesity
Values or Distributions in Source: Social jetlag (misalignment between biological clock and social schedule) is measured in hours of deviation from natural sleep timing
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Social jetlag of 2+ hours is associated with fatigue depression and burnout in working populations
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(3.5 to 6.0) | Medium: uniform(1.5 to 3.5) | Low: uniform(0 to 1.5)
Evidence-Based or Assumption: Partially evidence-based — 2-hour threshold from Roenneberg; 3.5-hour High Risk boundary is author assumption
Notes: Roenneberg reports clinically significant effects at 2+ hours social jetlag. The 3.5-hour threshold for High Risk provides a conservative buffer above this finding. Link: https://www.cell.com/current-biology/fulltext/S0960-9822(12)00534-5

Feature Definition: Schedule drift from established login baseline.
Published Source: Wittmann et al. — Social jetlag: Misalignment of biological and social time
Values or Distributions in Source: Social jetlag defined as difference between mid-sleep on work days vs free days; commonly 1-2 hours
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Circadian misalignment causes fatigue mood disturbance and reduced cognitive performance
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(3.5 to 6.0) | Medium: uniform(1.5 to 3.5) | Low: uniform(0 to 1.5)

Feature Definition: Ratio of tasks completed to tasks assigned within the monitoring window. NOTE: This feature was REMOVED from all Kaggle-based experiments due to target leakage (derived from Burn Rate). It exists only in the synthetic Part B dataset.
Published Source: Leiter and Maslach — Burnout and engagement: Contributions to a new vision
Values or Distributions in Source: The Maslach Burnout Inventory measures reduced personal accomplishment as one of three burnout dimensions
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Declining task completion rate is a documented behavioural indicator of reduced professional efficacy
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(8 to 38) | Medium: uniform(38 to 68) | Low: uniform(68 to 100)
Evidence-Based or Assumption: Partially evidence-based — directional relationship confirmed; specific thresholds are assumptions
Notes: IMPORTANT: This feature was REMOVED from Kaggle experiments due to target leakage. Formula (1-BurnRate)*100 creates direct leakage because label also comes from BurnRate. Used only in synthetic Part B data. Link: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213058616300043

Feature Definition: Ratio of completed to assigned tasks.
Published Source: WHO — Burn-out as occupational phenomenon: ICD-11
Values or Distributions in Source: Burnout defined by three dimensions: exhaustion; cynicism/depersonalisation; reduced professional efficacy
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Reduced professional efficacy (output) is a defining diagnostic criterion of occupational burnout
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(8 to 38) | Medium: uniform(38 to 68) | Low: uniform(68 to 100)
Notes: Link: https://www.who.int/news/item/28-05-2019-burn-out-an-occupational-phenomenon-international-classification-of-diseases. NOTE: Feature removed from Kaggle experiments due to target leakage.

Feature Definition: Ratio of completed to assigned tasks.
Published Source: Hemp — Presenteeism: At work but out of it
Values or Distributions in Source: Burned-out employees complete only 30-40% of expected output while appearing to work normal hours — a phenomenon called presenteeism
Relationship to Burnout Reported: Presenteeism causes 57.5 billion dollars annual productivity loss in the US; task completion is the primary measurable indicator
Formula Used in Synthetic Code: High Risk: uniform(8 to 38) | Medium: uniform(38 to 68) | Low: uniform(68 to 100)
Notes: Low Risk ceiling of 68% aligns with Harvard Business Review finding that even healthy workers rarely achieve 100% task completion due to context switching. Link: https://hbr.org/2004/10/presenteeism-at-work-but-out-of-it. NOTE: Feature removed from Kaggle experiments.
